arXiv:2605.04047v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum repeater chains build long-distance entanglement for quantum key distribution (QKD) by creating pairs on short links and joining them through entanglement swapping. Because stored pairs lose fidelity while they wait, swap timing can affect the secret-key rate. We study how network-layer swap scheduling affects six-state QKD on a simulated four-hop chain under an idealized Werner-state noise model. We compare a sequential (swap-and-wait) discipline, which builds and stores partial chains, with a synchronized (wait-and-swap) discipline, which waits until all links are ready before swapping. item.title: Asymmetric quantum Rabi model, trap-dipole resonance, and quantum gates with optically trapped ultracold polar molecules
item.description:
📚 Quantum Science and Technology
👤 Yan Lu and Xiao-Feng Shi
Optically trapped ultracold polar molecules can have multiple long-lived states for coding quantum information, and can exhibit electric dipole-dipole interactions (DDI) which enable entanglement generation. The general understanding on the quantized motion (QM) of optically trapped molecules is that it causes fluctuation of DDI. Here, we find that the molecular QM can realize an asymmetric quantum Rabi model, which is of specific importance in the study of fundamental physics. The molecular QM can also lead to an exotic trap-dipole resonance, resulting in excess population loss to uncoupled motional states, and, hence, should be avoided in a general quantum control over polar molecules. item.title: Quantum LDPC Codes from Polynomial Minors
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Vahid Nourozi, Roxana Smarandache, David G. M. Mitchell
arXiv:2610.19459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct quantum codes from codewords of a cyclic code and the minors of a polynomial matrix. The construction uses a two-row, three-column matrix whose minors yield a second matrix satisfying the CSS orthogonality condition. We derive the code dimension from the greatest common divisors of the entries and minors, with a simplified formula for odd lifting factors. A residue characterization identifies additional common factors of the minors and leads to a method for controlling the dimension through polynomial selection. We also give a condition for changing the minor generator without changing the code. Explicit polynomial constructions yield 13 quantum codes with verified minimum distances, including a [[255,80,12]] code of rate 80/255.

item.title: Quantum Work Statistics from Entanglement-Assisted Invariance
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Akira Sone, Akram Touil, Emery Doucet, Sebastian Deffner
arXiv:2610.20528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that the one-time measurement scheme is more consistent than the standard two-time measurement scheme with respect to the fundamental symmetry of entanglement, namely entanglement-assisted invariance (envariance). In particular, the work statistics obtained from the one-time measurement scheme arise naturally as a direct consequence of envariance for any driving unitary, without involving an explicit measurement postulate, whereas the analogous identification for the two-time measurement scheme is possible only for a Haar-measure-zero set of unitaries. This envariance-based formulation eliminates the ambiguity in work statistics related to the energetic cost of measurement.

item.title: Renormalisation of Quantum Cellular Automata
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Lorenzo Siro Trezzini, Alessandro Bisio, Paolo Perinotti
arXiv:2407.12652v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a coarse-graining procedure for quantum cellular automata on hypercubic lattices that consists in grouping neighboring cells into tiles and selecting a subspace within each tile. This is done in such a way that multiple evolution steps applied to this subspace can be viewed as a single evolution step of a new quantum cellular automaton, whose cells are the subspaces themselves. We derive a necessary and sufficient condition for renormalizability and use it to investigate the renormalization flow of cellular automata on a line, where the cells are qubits and the tiles are composed of two neighboring cells. The problem is exhaustively solved, and the fixed points of the renormalization flow are highlighted.

item.title: Spatial Phase Control of Energy and Ergotropy in Quantum Batteries
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Maryam Hadipour, Soroush Haseli
arXiv:2602.18192v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the role of spatial geometry in controlling energy storage and work extraction in a non-Markovian quantum battery. The system consists of two identical two-level systems coupled to a structured waveguide reservoir, where one qubit serves as the charger and the other as the battery. The spatial separation between the qubits introduces a geometry-dependent phase that governs collective interference, directly modulating the decay channels and energy transfer dynamics. We show that tuning the interqubit distance allows for the engineering of bright and dark collective pathways, which, in conjunction with environmental memory, significantly enhances the charging power, maximal stored energy, and ergotropy revivals.

item.title: Acoustic scattering from quantum dynamics
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Farhang Loran, Ali Mostafazadeh
arXiv:2610.19873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scattering of sound waves propagating in a compressible fluid is linked to the quantum dynamics generated by a class of non-Hermitian Hamiltonian operators. The scattering amplitude is expressed in terms of the corresponding evolution operator. This is used to provide a new proof of the reciprocity theorem in acoustic scattering, conduct analytic low-frequency acoustic scattering calculations, and study the scattering of sound waves by a finite planar array of delta-function point scatters embedded in an infinite acoustic slab. A detailed discussion of acoustic scattering properties of a homogeneous acoustic slab including a pair of delta-function point scatters on one of its faces is provided.
